summary: Express's own final handler still writes body-parser/status errors (e.g. malformed JSON, 400) to stderr via console.error as unstructured text, outside the logger and without requestId. Node's JSON.parse message can echo a snippet of the request body ("Unexpected token ..., \"{not json B\"... is not valid JSON"), so a body fragment can reach stderr. server.ts only owns the no-status branch; status errors are passed to next(err) unchanged by design (client response must not change).
evidence: apps/api/src/composition/request-log.test.ts redaction test: POST /ask with body '{not json ...' prints a SyntaxError stack to stderr from body-parser during the test run.
fix_direction: Add an explicit handler for status-carrying errors that logs structured (message scrubbed/omitted) with requestId and then responds with the same status/body as Express's default; needs a decision on the client body (default page leaks stack outside production).

summary: Other apps/api code (routes, indexing, ingest-store, whatsapp/store) still uses console.*; those lines bypass redaction and requestId. Left for the route lanes; routes can use req.log.
fix_direction: Replace with req.log / logger from composition/logger.ts.
